skills.name: Carry out basic calculations with moles, mass, particles and gas volume

note.text:
Three relations link a mole to things that can be measured.
• moles = mass ÷ molar mass, so mass = moles × molar mass.
• number of particles = moles × 6.02 × 10²³.
• volume of a gas at s.t.p. = moles × 22.4 dm³, so moles = volume ÷ 22.4.
Always write down what is given, change it to moles, and then change the moles to what is asked for.
Example: 11 g of carbon dioxide. Molar mass 44 g/mol, so moles = 11 ÷ 44 = 0.25 mol; volume at s.t.p. = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 dm³; molecules = 0.25 × 6.02 × 10²³.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to change between mass, moles, number of particles and gas volume in any direction.
Builds on: Lesson {20} (the mole and the Avogadro constant) and Lesson {19} (molar mass and molar volume).
Leads to: Lessons {22} to {27}, where these steps are used inside larger calculations.

Worked examples

key_words.meaning: the mass of one mole, in g/mol
standard temperature and pressure: {0} °C and one atmosphere
a cubic decimetre, the same as a litre

examples: {0.5} mol of gas = {11.2} dm³ at s.t.p.

mistake.why: Check with a simple case: {44} g of {formula('CO2')} must be {1} mol, and {44} ÷ {44} = {1}.

worked_example.problem: Find the number of moles in {m} g of {formula(F)}, and the volume it would fill at s.t.p.
steps: The molar mass of {formula(F)} is {molarMass(F)} g/mol.
moles = mass ÷ molar mass = {m} ÷ {molarMass(F)} = {molesOf(m, F)} mol.

example: {0.25} mol of a gas fills {5.6} dm³

check.prompt: What volume, in dm³ at s.t.p., is filled by {m} g of {formula(F)} gas?

misconceptions.explain: Change the mass to MOLES first, then multiply by {22.4}.

questions.prompt: How many moles are there in {m} g of {formula(F)}?

misconceptions.explain: Divide the mass by the molar mass.
moles = mass ÷ molar mass, not molar mass ÷ mass.

questions.prompt: What is the mass, in grams, of {n} mol of {formula(F)}?

misconceptions.explain: {molarMass(F)} g is one mole; here there are {n} mol.

questions.prompt: What volume, in dm³ at s.t.p., is filled by {m} g of {formula(F)} gas?

misconceptions.explain: Change the mass to MOLES first, then multiply by {22.4}.

questions.prompt: What mass, in grams, of {formula(F)} gas fills {v} dm³ at s.t.p.?

misconceptions.explain: Change the volume to MOLES first: divide by {22.4}.
Divide the volume by {22.4}; do not multiply.

questions.prompt: How many moles of {formula(F)} hold {p} times the Avogadro number of molecules?

misconceptions.explain: The Avogadro number IS one mole: no further multiplying is needed.
{p} times the number of particles is {p} times the number of moles.

solution: The Avogadro number of molecules is {1} mol.
